subject: Data quality for driver safety models
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently onboarded Motive away from their in-house tools as they moved from frame-based to video annotation. Like many driver safety teams, they faced challenges around handling billions of miles of in-cab and dashcam footage, e.g. surfacing relevant driver behaviours and maintaining temporal consistency for high quality video datasets. 

I imagine [COMPANY] is also working towards more accurate driver safety models, have you run into similar challenges? Sharing a few bullets on why Motive moved to Encord: 
Model-assisted labelling to cut down repetitive frame-by-frame work Consolidated platform for curation and annotation to reduce tooling overhead Org and project-level analytics to track data quality and annotation efficiency How are you approaching training data preparation at [COMPANY]? I'm flexible Tuesdays to Thursdays if you're open to bouncing some ideas.

subject: your annotation pipeline can be more scalable
text:
Hi [NAME],

We just onboarded Mytra who was scaling up real-world data collection for their perception models. Noticed Mech is piloting in Japan - curious if you've run into similar challenges with surging data volume at Dexterity? 

Mytra came to Encord to more efficiently index, auto-label and QA for messy data from the physical world. They use our model-assisted automation to scale their annotation pipeline, alongside capabilities to curate and validate label accuracy across 2D (image & video) and 3D point cloud data in one place. (+ we also complement well with your existing visualization/debugging tool Foxglove.)

Open to swap notes on scaling annotation pipeline w/ messy real-world data?

subject: Data development - dashcam videos
text:
Hi [NAME],

Noticed you've been automating video annotation with VLMs. One challenge
we've seen (for example with Motive) is that breaking videos into frames
creates friction for higher-order tasks - e.g. keeping temporal
consistency, captioning across timelines, or relating annotated objects to
specific driver behaviors.

Curious how are you approaching those bottlenecks at [COMPANY]? We've been
working on a workflow orchestration system to maintain consistency across
long-form video and multi-step review processes, and I'd love to compare
notes.

Would you be open to a quick chat?

subject: Data development - dashcam videos
text:
Hi [NAME],

Noticed you lead the video analytics team to detect relevant events from
dashcam videos - we just onboarded Motive on very similar use case. Keen to
hear if you've come across similar challenges?

For context - Motive was looking for a more scalable annotation system as
they moved from frame-based to video annotation. Encord helps them improve
labelling efficiency by:

   1. Surfacing rare events from million miles of driving videos through
   filtering, natural language and embedding search
   2. Enabling model-assisted workflow to auto-label / caption relevant
   objects & event before human review + capabilities to render and
   interpolate annotations across video natively

Open to see how we're making detection, segmentation and captioning tasks
~5x more efficient? Can demo on a workflow that mirrors yours at [COMPANY] -
lmk.
